anydesk_cache.what: AnyDesk's config and trace folders: user.conf/system.conf (settings, ID/alias), ad.trace logs, connection_trace.txt.
anydesk_cache.used_for: Deleting can reset AnyDesk settings and, for portable use, its ID.
anydesk_cache.risk: Lost settings, address book, possibly a new AnyDesk ID; lost logs.
anydesk_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

anydesk_thumbnails.what: Not documented by the vendor. Thumbnail images AnyDesk shows for recent sessions.
anydesk_thumbnails.used_for: Recreated after the next connection to each machine.

discord_cache.what: Discord's Chromium/Electron disk caches: HTTP cache (Cache), compiled JavaScript (Code Cache) and compiled GPU shaders (GPUCache).
discord_cache.used_for: Speeds up loading the app's interface. Rebuilt automatically on next start; the first launch is a little slower.
discord_cache.risk: None known; login token lives in Local Storage, which is not touched. First start slightly slower.
discord_cache.before_cleaning: Quit Discord completely (also from the tray)

discord_canary_cache.what: The HTTP Cache folder of Discord Canary and Discord PTB (test builds).
discord_canary_cache.used_for: Speeds up loading the app's interface. Rebuilt automatically on next start; the first launch is a little slower.
discord_canary_cache.risk: None known; login in Local Storage is untouched.
discord_canary_cache.catalog_concern: Description mentions 'crash reports' - the path is only Cache.

discord_developer_logs.what: Not documented by the vendor. Discord desktop's log folder.
discord_developer_logs.used_for: Diagnostics only; new logs are written as Discord runs.

discord_full_cache.what: Discord's Chromium/Electron disk caches: HTTP cache (Cache), compiled JavaScript (Code Cache) and compiled GPU shaders (GPUCache). Also blob_storage (Chromium Blob store).
discord_full_cache.used_for: Speeds up loading the app's interface. Rebuilt automatically on next start; the first launch is a little slower.
discord_full_cache.risk: blob_storage is managed storage rather than a plain cache; small risk of breaking data the app references. Login (Local Storage) is not touched.
discord_full_cache.catalog_concern: Catalog says 'safe'. Same blob_storage concern as slack_cache_full; overlaps discord_cache paths (double counting).

element_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Element's whole data folder, including the encryption keys store (IndexedDB) for Matrix end-to-end encryption.
element_cache.used_for: Deleting signs out and can lose message keys.
element_cache.risk: Sign-out and possibly permanent loss of encrypted message history without key backup.
element_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

mattermost_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. %APPDATA%\Mattermost is the desktop app's whole data folder (server list, sessions, Local Storage).
mattermost_cache.used_for: Deleting signs you out and removes servers.
mattermost_cache.risk: Sign-out; lost server list and settings.
mattermost_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

microsoft_teams_full_cache.what: Classic Teams' Cache, blob_storage and GPUCache folders under %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Teams, and %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Teams\Cache.
microsoft_teams_full_cache.used_for: Microsoft documents clearing everything in %appdata%\Microsoft\Teams for classic Teams; it rebuilds. Classic Teams is retired, so this is often leftovers.
microsoft_teams_full_cache.risk: Slower first start; no sign-in loss from these subfolders.

ms_teams_npc_cache.what: The whole LocalCache of a Teams package (MSTeamsNPC*), which contains WebView2 profiles with IndexedDB/Local Storage.
ms_teams_npc_cache.used_for: Deleting it amounts to resetting Teams.
ms_teams_npc_cache.risk: Sign-out and loss of personalization, like an app reset.
ms_teams_npc_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right; only the Cache subfolders are safe (see teams_new_webview_cache).

mumble_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Mumble client and overlay log folders.

mumble_full_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Mumble's whole data folders, including mumble.sqlite (favourite servers, settings) and your certificate (your identity on servers).
mumble_full_cache.used_for: Deleting loses your identity certificate - registered usernames on servers can no longer be claimed.
mumble_full_cache.risk: Permanent loss of Mumble identity certificate and settings.
mumble_full_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

nomachine_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. %APPDATA%\NoMachine holds connection files and settings.
nomachine_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

parsec_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Parsec 'logs' and 'cache' subfolders; Parsec's config.txt/config.json and sign-in are in %APPDATA%\Parsec itself, not these.

rdp_cache.what: Remote Desktop Connection's persistent bitmap cache (bcache*.bmc, Cache*.bin): screen tiles from past RDP sessions.
rdp_cache.used_for: mstsc reuses cached tiles to draw remote screens faster; rebuilt during the next session. Clearing also removes a privacy/forensic trace.
rdp_cache.risk: Slightly slower first redraw in the next RDP session.
rdp_cache.catalog_concern: Description ('clipboard temp and redirected drive cache') is wrong: it is the bitmap cache.

remote_desktop_cache.what: The whole Terminal Server Client folder; here it contains only the bitmap Cache folder.
remote_desktop_cache.risk: Slower first redraw; the folder itself is recreated.
remote_desktop_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling is conservative but defensible; it duplicates rdp_cache. Saved RDP credentials are in Credential Manager and Default.rdp in Documents - neither is here.

signal_cache.what: Signal Desktop's Electron HTTP Cache and its logs folder. Messages are in Signal\sql (encrypted database) with its key in config.json - not targeted.
signal_cache.used_for: Cache rebuilds on start; logs are diagnostics (used for Signal debug logs).
signal_cache.risk: Lost diagnostics only. Deleting sql, config.json or attachments.noindex would lose all messages - never target them.
signal_cache.catalog_concern: Description mentions 'attachment temp and sticker downloads' - not in these paths, and Signal attachments are user data.

skype_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. A cache folder of the (retired) Skype desktop app.
skype_cache.used_for: Temporary data refetched by Skype. Microsoft retired Skype in May 2025.
skype_cache.risk: None known for a cache folder.
skype_cache.catalog_concern: Description mentions 'shared files temp' - not documented.

skype_for_business_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor here. The Lync folders hold the Skype for Business sign-in info folder (sip_*), contact cache and logs.
skype_for_business_cache.used_for: Microsoft's sign-in fixes delete the sip_ folder deliberately, which forces re-download of contacts and re-sign-in.
skype_for_business_cache.risk: Sign-in information and local conversation/contact cache reset.
skype_for_business_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right for an automatic clean: it resets sign-in. Description ('meeting recordings') is wrong.

slack_cache.what: Slack's Chromium/Electron disk caches: HTTP cache (Cache), compiled JavaScript (Code Cache) and compiled GPU shaders (GPUCache).
slack_cache.used_for: Speeds up loading the app's interface. Rebuilt automatically on next start; the first launch is a little slower.
slack_cache.risk: None known; sign-in lives in Local Storage/IndexedDB, not touched. Slack's own 'Clear Cache and Restart' does the same.
slack_cache.before_cleaning: Quit Slack completely (also from the tray)

slack_cache_full.what: Slack's Chromium/Electron disk caches: HTTP cache (Cache), compiled JavaScript (Code Cache) and compiled GPU shaders (GPUCache). Also blob_storage: Chromium's on-disk store for Blob data used by the web app.
slack_cache_full.used_for: Speeds up loading the app's interface. Rebuilt automatically on next start; the first launch is a little slower. blob_storage is managed by Chromium's storage system, not a plain cache.
slack_cache_full.risk: blob_storage may back data the app still references (e.g. queued uploads, IndexedDB blobs); deleting it can make such data unreadable. Gain is usually small.
slack_cache_full.catalog_concern: Catalog says 'safe'. blob_storage is not a documented rebuildable cache; Cache/Code Cache/GPUCache alone ('slack_cache') are safe. Duplicates slack_cache's paths (double counting).

sunshine_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Sunshine normally writes sunshine.log next to its config in %ProgramFiles%\Sunshine\config; %APPDATA%\Sunshine\logs is not documented.
sunshine_cache.catalog_concern: Path likely matches nothing; never target Sunshine's config folder (sunshine.conf, apps.json, paired clients).

teams_cache.what: Classic Teams' Cache, blob_storage and GPUCache (Roaming) plus a Local Cache folder.
teams_cache.used_for: Microsoft's own fix is to delete everything in %appdata%\Microsoft\Teams for classic Teams; it is rebuilt.
teams_cache.risk: Slower first start; classic Teams is retired, so this is usually leftovers.
teams_cache.catalog_concern: Disabled only as a duplicate of 'microsoft_teams_full_cache' - correct.

teams_new_webview_cache.what: New Teams' WebView2 Cache/Code Cache/GPUCache for every profile, plus its Logs folder.
teams_new_webview_cache.used_for: Microsoft documents deleting files in the new Teams cache folder; caches rebuild. Logs are diagnostics used by support.
teams_new_webview_cache.risk: Teams' Logs folder is diagnostics: once deleted, a problem that already happened can no longer be investigated (Microsoft's clear-cache article warns of this). The caches themselves rebuild; sign-in stays (IndexedDB/Local Storage untouched).

teamspeak5_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. TeamSpeak 5's whole data folders, including identities and settings.
teamspeak5_cache.used_for: Deleting can lose your TeamSpeak identity.
teamspeak5_cache.risk: Lost identity (server permissions tied to it) and settings.
teamspeak5_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

teamspeak_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. TeamSpeak 3 / TeamSpeak log folders.
teamspeak_cache.catalog_concern: Description mentions 'client query interface' - unrelated to logs.

teamviewer_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor here. %APPDATA%\TeamViewer* hold connection logs and per-user settings/partner data.
teamviewer_cache.used_for: Deletion resets TeamViewer settings and history.
teamviewer_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

telegram_cache.what: Telegram Desktop keeps its cache under %APPDATA%\Telegram Desktop\tdata\user_data (media cache) and tdata\emoji. The catalog's 'cache' and 'emoji' folders directly under 'Telegram Desktop' are not where it stores them.
telegram_cache.used_for: Media/emoji caches are re-downloaded from Telegram's servers when needed.
telegram_cache.risk: For the real cache: re-downloads only. Everything else in tdata (key_datas, session files) is the login - never delete it.
telegram_cache.catalog_concern: Paths likely match nothing (cache is inside tdata\user_data). Description says 'session data' - wrong and alarming: session data is the login. If corrected, target only tdata\user_data and tdata\emoji, never tdata.

viber_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. A 'cache' folder in ViberPC; chat history is in ViberPC\<phone number>\viber.db.
viber_cache.used_for: Presumably media/thumbnail cache refetched as needed.
viber_cache.risk: Low for 'cache'. Never widen to ViberPC or the phone-number folder: that deletes message history and forces re-activation.
viber_cache.catalog_concern: Undocumented subfolder; acceptable only as a named cache folder.

vnc_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Per-user data of RealVNC/TightVNC/UltraVNC: settings, address books, possibly saved passwords and sign-in.
vnc_cache.risk: Lost address books, settings, RealVNC sign-in.
vnc_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.

whatsapp_cache.what: The HTTP Cache folder of the old Electron WhatsApp Desktop (%LOCALAPPDATA%\WhatsApp).
whatsapp_cache.used_for: Speeds up loading the app's interface. Rebuilt automatically on next start; the first launch is a little slower.
whatsapp_cache.risk: None known; login lives in that profile's IndexedDB/Local Storage, which is not targeted.
whatsapp_cache.catalog_concern: Legacy app; current WhatsApp is the Store app (see whatsapp_store_webview_cache).

whatsapp_store_webview_cache.what: Cache, Code Cache and GPUCache of the WhatsApp Store app's WebView2 profile.
whatsapp_store_webview_cache.used_for: Speeds up loading the app's interface. Rebuilt automatically on next start; the first launch is a little slower.
whatsapp_store_webview_cache.risk: None known; IndexedDB/Local Storage (login, messages) in the same profile are not targeted.

whatsapp_uwp_cache.what: The whole LocalCache of the WhatsApp Store app, which includes its WebView2 profile's IndexedDB and Local Storage - where the login and messages live.
whatsapp_uwp_cache.used_for: Deleting it signs WhatsApp out and drops local chats until re-linked.
whatsapp_uwp_cache.risk: Sign-out; must re-link with phone; local chat history lost. This happened on this machine (CLAUDE.md).
whatsapp_uwp_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right. Only EBWebView\Default\Cache, Code Cache, GPUCache are safe.

zoom_cache.what: Zoom's per-user data lives in %APPDATA%\Zoom (logs in %APPDATA%\Zoom\logs). These %LOCALAPPDATA%\Zoom cache/thumbnail/logs folders are not documented.
zoom_cache.used_for: Logs are diagnostics; thumbnails/caches would be refetched.
zoom_cache.risk: These %LOCALAPPDATA%\Zoom folders are not documented by Zoom, so what else they hold cannot be confirmed; logs are diagnostics. Local recordings are in Documents\Zoom and are not targeted.
zoom_cache.catalog_concern: Paths are under %LOCALAPPDATA% while Zoom uses %APPDATA%; likely finds nothing. Description ('meeting recordings temp files') is misleading.

zoom_recordings_cache.what: Despite the label, the path is a Zoom logs folder (%LOCALAPPDATA%\Zoom\logs), not recordings.
zoom_recordings_cache.risk: Lost diagnostics; no recordings are touched.
zoom_recordings_cache.catalog_concern: Label/description say 'recordings' - misleading; a user may fear losing recordings or expect space from them. Duplicates zoom_cache's logs path. Zoom documents logs under %APPDATA%\Zoom\logs.

zulip_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. %APPDATA%\Zulip is the whole Electron data folder.
zulip_cache.catalog_concern: Disabling was right: the path is the app's whole data folder, which holds settings, sign-in tokens or keys, not a cache.
